test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They worked / very hardly / on their project / for several weeks.
solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. very hardly .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **“hardly”** is incorrect in this context. **"Hardly"** means "barely" or "almost not," which does not fit the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• The correct word to use here is **"hard."** The phrase should be *"They worked very hard on their project."*
 
• The error lies in the misuse of the adverb **"hardly."**

Correct sentence: *They worked very hard on their project for several weeks*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Difference between "hard" and "hardly":**

 
 
• **Hard:** An adverb that means "with a lot of effort." Example: She worked hard to complete the assignment.
 
• **Hardly:** An adverb that means "barely" or "almost not." Example: He hardly slept last night.
 
 
 
• Using **"very hardly"** is grammatically incorrect because **"hardly"** already expresses a limiting degree, and "very" cannot modify it in this context.
